rationale.conceptual: The method is established DFT benchmarking, but requires careful implementation of multiple property calculations (geometry, frequencies, polarizabilities, interaction energies, delocalization error, exciton stability, torsion scans) and correct derivation of error metrics against a double-hybrid reference. Non-trivial but no novel algorithms; domain expertise needed.
rationale.execution: Multi-stage pipeline with heavy job orchestration: prepare molecules, run reference DSD-PBEP86 at two basis-set levels, run 17 functionals on all property classes, perform fractional electron scans and torsion scans, then aggregate errors into JSON. Many load-bearing handoffs and data management steps; fragile if not properly scripted.

difficulty.reasoning: The task is a DFT benchmarking study requiring running many standard but computationally heavy quantum chemistry calculations with Psi4, aggregating error metrics. Conceptual difficulty is moderate (established multi-property benchmarking). Execution is high due to orchestrating 17 functionals × multiple molecular systems, managing large numbers of jobs and aggregating results.

compute_estimate.reasoning: Density functional calculations on small molecules (PEDOT trimers, hexamers) with jun-cc-pVDZ basis; 17 functionals plus double-hybrid reference. CPU-intensive but limited data volume; peak RAM moderate for large molecules but overall small systems. No GPU acceleration required.
